gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of its three picks can take an add-on battery. Only the BLUETTI AC70 can: BLUETTI lists the B80, B230 and B300 for it. Anker's US page says the C1000 Gen 2 'does not include an expansion feature', and EcoFlow's US FAQ says the RIVER 2 series does 'not support an Extra Battery'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited bluettipower.com/products/ac70 page and its ?variant= copy. They show an 'AC70+B80+Aviation to XT60 cable' bundle (1,574 Wh, $898) and 'Seamless UPS in 20ms', but they never list which batteries are compatible, and they say nothing about B230/B300 or about rival units being fixed-capacity. ChatGPT also opened the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max product pages, the EU manual and the brochure, plus powerstationsize.com and 326energy.com/compare, but none of them is cited. That FAQ page lists the extra-battery question on the same page ChatGPT got, yet the answer never uses it. So the rivals have part of the AC70 side and none of the exclusions. ChatGPT's answer calls the C1000 Gen 2 'Best for longer outages' and never says its 1,024 Wh is the ceiling.
decides: If the shopper wants more TV hours later, for long outages or a bigger TV, the AC70 is the only one of ChatGPT's three picks that can grow. The AC70 page lists a B80 bundle at 1,574 Wh, and BLUETTI's AC70 page names B230 (2,048 Wh) and B300 (3,072 Wh) as compatible. The C1000 Gen 2 stops at 1,024 Wh and the RIVER 2 Max stays at its built-in capacity. Anker's BP1000 add-on battery is not a way out: its maker page lists only the C1000 and C1000X. For a fixed TV-runtime need that fits in 1 kWh, this changes nothing. The C1000 Gen 2 still has the faster UPS switchover (10 ms vs 20 ms), which matters if the TV or streaming box should stay on when the power cuts.
